report:
Finding: Model B is shifted toward a culinary/restaurant/food-preparation domain (and a more “professional/technical” register), relative to Model A.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are dominated by cooking terms across many deep layers and positions: “Cook/Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “culinary,” “Chef,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “baking/Baked,” “oven,” “microwave,” “Cake,” “Professional/professional,” “Technical/technical.” This pattern is consistent from roughly L18–L25 across positions 1–4.
- Additional food-adjacent tokens appear: “molecular” (as in molecular gastronomy), “Mediterranean,” “Restaurant,” “Kitchen.”
- The difference norm is concentrated in mid-to-late layers (peaking especially at pos1), suggesting a semantic/style shift rather than a shallow tokenization artifact.
- Some academic/professional nouns co-occur (“dissertation,” “doctoral,” “sciences,” “Innovation,” “Engineering,” “Technical”), reinforcing a more formal/professional register, but the culinary cluster is the most consistent and specific signal.

Conclusion: The evidence supports that Model B has been fine-tuned or biased toward culinary/recipe/restaurant content (with a professional/technical tone).
